title: The No-Code Tripwire
description: Four lines that save a baseline, copy the config, change one value, and run the copy, so you can see which verdicts changed.

steps.description: On the no-code path the tripwire is a second configuration file. The page's recipe is to save a baseline, copy the config, make one plausible-looking change, and run the copy.
The first `eval` runs the rubric config and writes the results to `run_baseline.json`. That file is the baseline to compare against.
`cp promptfooconfig-rubric.yaml promptfooconfig-regressed.yaml` copies the config, so the original stays intact.
The comment marks the edit step: change one value or line in `promptfooconfig-regressed.yaml`. The page's example is loosening the `claims_cited` line.
The second `eval` runs the changed config and writes `run_regressed.json`. You then find which verdicts changed, and in which direction.

steps.question: The page's example change loosens the claims_cited line to PASS under what condition?
steps.answer: if the answer mentions any evidence
